summary: Compare demanded pulley torque with available belt traction without inventing a post-slip speed.
objective: Expose the authoritative model and its visible response: flat-belt traction bound before slip.
applies_when: Flexible massless flat belt in cylindrical contact, positive lower-side tension Tlo, static friction coefficient mu>=0 and wrap beta in radians; quasi-static traction feasibility only.
intent_signals: Compare demanded pulley torque with available belt traction without inventing a post-slip speed.
example_prompts: Build an inspectable demonstration of flat-belt traction bound before slip with parameter controls and a reset.
negative_signals: Not V-belts, toothed belts, belt stretch, centrifugal tension, wear or post-slip dynamics.
not_for: Not V-belts, toothed belts, belt stretch, centrifugal tension, wear or post-slip dynamics.

principles: No-slip motion is a conditional ideal constraint, not evidence that any requested torque can be transmitted.
The static bound identifies loss of sticking feasibility; it is not a kinetic friction or slip-rate equation.
implementation: Own finite Tlo>0 and demanded Thi>=Tlo in N, finite mu>=0 dimensionless, finite unsigned contact angle beta>=0 in rad and finite radius R>0 in m. beta is the magnitude of the contacted arc, never a signed rotation sweep; beta=0 is the no-contact limiting case. Compare log(Thi/Tlo) with mu*beta, using a declared numerical tolerance and showing equality as the limiting case. Torque magnitude is (Thi-Tlo)*R in N m.

Draw the actual contacted arc and tangential tension arrows; beta must match that arc. In a multi-pulley drive check every contact with its own mu,beta,R. Treat Tlo as an explicit input rather than inferring it from unloaded pretension.

A separate ideal transmission mode may prescribe matching belt and rim tangential velocity. Beyond the static limit show demand exceeds bound and stop claiming sticking; do not animate an inferred slipping speed. Parameter changes recompute all labels and reset restores the initial demand.
observable_checks: At mu=0 or beta=0 the bound permits only Thi=Tlo. At mu=0.3,beta=pi,Tlo=100 N the threshold is approximately 256.63 N; 250 N is below and 260 N above.
Increasing wrap with fixed tensions increases the margin. Swapping which physical side is tight must update arrows and torque direction without treating negative tension as compression.

known_limits: Not V-belts, toothed belts, belt stretch, centrifugal tension, wear or post-slip dynamics.
Authored reusable guidance; no solver or rendered artifact has been tested for this record.
creative_affordances: Use a cutaway, restrained ghost reference or annotated section only when it clarifies the modeled relation; a planar diagram remains valid when depth adds no information.

claims.statement: For the stated flat-belt model, the maximum larger tension before slip is Tlo exp(mu beta), with beta measured in radians. The net pulley torque magnitude is the tension difference times pulley radius; each contact must satisfy its own traction bound.
claims.scope: Flexible massless flat belt in cylindrical contact, positive lower-side tension Tlo, static friction coefficient mu>=0 and wrap beta in radians; quasi-static traction feasibility only.

source_refs.locator: Friction in Flat Belts, equation 1; Torque and Power Transmission in Belt-Driven Systems
